report.summary:
Screened all 52 clients with client_updates, client_performance (round 20), drift_by_round, feature_summary (round 20), and subgroup_outcomes for Sex, AgeGroup and Income, then ran narrower confirmation queries. No client showed a consistent, multi-tool fault pattern, so no findings are submitted.

Updates (c2): no size-adjusted flags for any client. Mean cosines are all positive (lowest GA 0.23, PR 0.25), and the minimum norm ratios of small clients (GU, VI) are consistent with their size. No sign of poisoning, free-riding or explanation instability.

Performance (c3): only GU had a flag (CITL z=-3.9, n=237). Pooled AUC is 0.82 and pooled CITL is 0.002. Nothing else stands out.

Drift (c4, c11): DC had a max_shift_sd z=+3.9 (DiffWalk), but its per-round shifts are sporadic rather than persistent. VI and GU show isolated spikes that return to zero, which is typical of noise on small clients, not a sustained shift from an onset round.

Features (c5, c10): the first screen flagged CT GenHlth p99 (z_noise 6.1), WV MentHlth p99 (z_noise -5.3) and several Sex/Stroke tail values. The narrower confirmation at epsilon 2 returned normal values for CT, WV, DC and GU (CT GenHlth p99 5.01; WV MentHlth p99 29.75), so these were noise. No sentinel-code pattern (0 or 99) was confirmed.

Subgroups (c6-c8): SC Sex FNR z_noise -3.5 is weak. Small-cell AgeGroup and Income outliers (DC 38 records, NH 102, TX 268) are within small-sample noise. No consistent under-diagnosis pattern.

Budget note: the attribution_churn call was made with epsilon 0 but still charged 1.0. Total spent is 20.0.
